help.title: Quick help
help.start.title: Getting started
help.start.1: Sign in: enter your login and password. Your teacher provides them. The sign-in is kept in this browser.
help.start.2: Create a project: "New project", "From example" (lessons and examples), "Open folder" or "Upload archive".
help.start.3: A project consists of design files (`.v`, `.sv`) and a pin constraint file (`.cst`). The file `fpgasim.json` is optional: the simulator creates it when you change settings.
help.start.4: An "in browser" project saves to the server by itself. "Export" gives a copy on disk: click the project name.
help.account.title: Sign-in and saving to the server
help.account.1: After you sign in on another computer, your projects appear in the list by themselves. The icon in the project row shows whether the project is saved on the server.
help.account.2: Without a server connection, editing and saving work. Changes stay in the browser and go to the server when the connection returns.
help.account.3: If one file was changed on two computers, the simulator shows both versions. Choose "Keep mine" or "Take server's".
help.account.4: A project opens in only one browser tab. A folder project is not saved to the server.
help.account.5: The button with your name on the projects screen opens a menu: "Change password" and "Sign out". Your teacher replaces a lost password.
help.account.6: A deleted project stays in the trash for 30 days. Your teacher can restore it.
help.build.title: Build
help.build.1: Click "Build" or press Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on Mac). The build runs on the server and takes a few seconds.
help.build.2: The "Messages" tab shows errors and warnings. Click a message: the editor goes to the line.
help.build.3: The simulator finds the top module and testbenches by itself. If there are several top modules, choose one in project settings: click the project name at the top left.
help.build.4: The label next to the "Build" button shows the build state. "Changed since build" means the simulation runs the previous build.
help.run.title: Simulation
help.run.1: "Run" starts the simulation. If the project is not built or changed since the build, "Run" builds it first. "Pause" stops the simulation, "Reset" returns the design to the start.
help.run.2: "Step" runs a set number of clocks, a set time, or until an output changes.
help.run.3: "Speed" sets the ratio of simulation time to real time. The number next to it shows the actual ratio.
help.run.4: The bottom bar shows simulation time and clock number.
help.board.title: Board and breadboard
help.board.1: The board drawing shows the board's LEDs and buttons. Press buttons S1 and S2 with the mouse. Shift+click keeps a button pressed.
help.board.2: The color of a header pin shows its state: free, used by a design port, forbidden. The hover hint names the pin.
help.board.3: "Part" places an LED, button, switch, UART, WS2812 strip or probe on the breadboard and connects the part to board pins.
help.board.4: "Binding" shows which design port is connected to which pin. With a `.cst` file, that file sets the binding.
help.board.5: Click the UART icon on the board to open the terminal: it shows bytes from the design and sends typed text to the design.
help.debug.title: Signals, waveforms, testbench
help.debug.1: The "Signals" tab: on the left, the design signal tree; on the right, the watch list with values. At first the tree has only ports. The "Show internal signals and rebuild" button adds the rest; simulation with them is slower.
help.debug.2: The "Record" button adds a signal to the recording. On the "Waveforms" tab, click "Record": the panel shows the chosen signals over time.
help.debug.3: The "Trigger" field starts recording on a condition: on an edge or a change of the chosen signal.
help.debug.4: The "Testbench" tab runs a testbench file (`tb_*.v`) on the server and shows its output. "Show waveform" opens the testbench VCD file.
help.debug.5: "Export VCD" saves the waveform as a file; GTKWave and Surfer open it.
help.folder.title: Folder on disk
help.folder.1: "Open folder" (Chrome and Edge) links the project to a folder on disk: files are read and written directly in the folder.
help.folder.2: Edit files in your own editor. With "Rebuild on change" checked, the simulator builds the project by itself.
help.folder.3: After a page reload, the browser asks for access again: click "Reopen folder".
help.limits.title: What the simulator does not show
help.limits.1: The simulator computes logic without delays. A design that works here may not meet timing on the board.
help.limits.2: The icon at the right end of the status bar opens the full list of limits.
